scope: Cache levels and capacity from dependent-load timing; shared-machine conditions; not blind specification inference.

capacity_estimates.evidence: 64 B random: 32 KiB medians 2.8672-2.9141 across three processes; 36 KiB 7.9297 TSC ticks/load.
64 B random: 256 KiB medians 8.0586-8.1133 across three processes; 288 KiB 13.8164; 512 KiB 22.8398-22.9102 TSC ticks/load.

capacity_estimates.interpretation: Broad layout-dependent effective transition under concurrent workloads, not a bound on physical LLC capacity.

excluded_runs.round1: Failed at 512 MiB MADV_COLLAPSE before that point was timed; 4 completed points retained separately.

caveats: CPU0 and CPU3 were 100% busy during every benchmark subprocess interval in both complete rounds.
1037 involuntary context switches in the two complete rounds; no measured faults or voluntary switches; all samples retained.

An initial unfiltered lscpu command exposed OS cache-size fields before reading the protocol; this experiment cannot be described as blind. Intervals and numerical conclusions are supported by the recorded timing curves. No PMU measurements were taken.
Empirical brackets are not confidence intervals; different layouts, page policies, batches and processes remain identifiable.
third_round: Not executed. Approximate L1D/L2 results and LLC uncertainty can be reported after the requested two rounds; narrower boundaries would require additional measured points.
